nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil fungi promotion_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How does the author plan to enhance the visibility of Kew Bulletin?
nodes.answer: The author plans to enhance the journal's online presence through regular social media posts to communicate the excitement and importance of plant and fungal taxonomy to a broader audience.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil fungi promotion_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Were there significant differences observed in fungal communities under manure treatments across growth stages?
nodes.answer: No significant differences in diversity or community structure were observed for fungal communities in manure treatments across different growth stages.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil fungi promotion_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are the keywords associated with this study?
nodes.answer: The keywords associated with this study are Rhizosphere microbes, Bacteria, Fungi, Growth stages, and Temporal stability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil fungi promotion_qna_003
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What were the two aims of the long-term field experiment characterized in the study?
nodes.answer: The study aimed to (i) determine whether organic fertilizer enhanced temporal variations in rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities, and (ii) assess the stability of both bacterial and fungal communities across different sorghum growth stages.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil fungi promotion_qna_004
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What four experimental treatments were manipulated in the study?
nodes.answer: The four experimental treatments manipulated were nitrogen availability, presence of fungal pathogens, functional composition of the vascular plant community, and vascular plant richness.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Soil health management|Soil fungi promotion_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How were the nitrogen availability and presence of fungal pathogens implemented in the experiment?
nodes.answer: Nitrogen availability was manipulated through fertilization, and the presence of fungal pathogens was manipulated through fungicide application.
